ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Marilyn Monroe Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: New patient with severe painful periods and pelvic pain: history and pelvic examination, suspected endometriosis, first-line hormonal and anti-inflammatory treatment, a pain plan without opioids or sedatives, and a depression and anxiety screen. Concerns: Her periods are so painful that she misses work, and she wants to know what is wrong; She wants children one day and is afraid that the cause of her pain, or an operation, will prevent it; She feels low and sleeps badly on painful nights, and does not want to depend on pills. [S]

tr.td: Naproxen 500 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth twice daily with food, from two days before an expected bleed until the third day, and for pain flares; no more than 10 days a month
One tablet by mouth twice daily with food when needed for pelvic pain
Ethinyl estradiol 0.02 mg and norethindrone acetate 1 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth daily, taken continuously without a pill-free week
One tablet by mouth daily, continuously
Nitrofurantoin (monohydrate and macrocrystals) 100 mg oral capsule, one capsule by mouth twice daily with food for 5 days
One capsule by mouth twice daily with food for 5 days
Folic acid 0.4 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth daily

list.item: Severe painful periods since her teens, worse over the past three years, with pelvic pain between periods, deep pain with intercourse, and painful bowel movements during periods; she misses work for two or three days each cycle. Tender, slightly fixed retroverted uterus with tenderness and fullness in the left adnexa and along the left uterosacral ligament. Suspected endometriosis; transvaginal ultrasound and gynecology consultation booked: resolved, confirmed [S]

Endometriosis: a 3.4 cm left ovarian endometrioma on transvaginal ultrasound, with a tender, thickened left uterosacral ligament and no deep nodule of the bowel or bladder seen; diagnosed from imaging and examination without surgery, as the ESHRE guideline allows. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented endometriosis: active, confirmed [S]

Major depressive disorder, single episode, moderate: about two months of low mood, poor sleep on painful nights, low energy, guilt about missed work, and poor concentration (PHQ-9 12, item 9 scored 0; GAD-7 8); Mood Disorder Questionnaire negative; no thoughts of suicide or self-harm: active, confirmed [S]

Acute uncomplicated cystitis: one day of burning, frequency and urgency with suprapubic discomfort, without fever, flank pain or blood in the urine; urine dipstick positive for leukocyte esterase and nitrite; culture grew Escherichia coli sensitive to nitrofurantoin; resolved: resolved, confirmed [S]

Pelvic floor muscle dysfunction with myofascial pain: deep pain with intercourse that persisted after three months of hormonal suppression, with tender, tight levator ani muscles that reproduce the pain on examination: active, confirmed [S]

tr.td: New patient with severe painful periods and pelvic pain: history and pelvic examination, suspected endometriosis, first-line hormonal and anti-inflammatory treatment, a pain plan without opioids or sedatives, and a depression and anxiety screen
Transvaginal ultrasound result and gynecology consultation: diagnosis, surgery, and fertility counseling
Three-month review on continuous hormonal treatment: pain, bleeding, mood, and pain with intercourse
Four-month review: pelvic floor physical therapy, follow-up ultrasound, mood, and pregnancy plans
Same-day sick visit for burning on urination

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: First-line treatment for suspected endometriosis without waiting for a diagnosis: naproxen with food for pain days, and a combined estrogen and progestin pill taken continuously to stop the periods, after a negative pregnancy test and a check for reasons to avoid estrogen (migraine with aura, smoking over 35, clotting history, high blood pressure)
Gynecology consultation for suspected endometriosis: diagnosis, the role and timing of surgery, and fertility counseling for a woman who wants children

Transvaginal ultrasound by an experienced sonographer, looking for endometriomas and deep nodules; CA-125 not used to diagnose endometriosis; gonorrhea and chlamydia tests and a urinalysis to exclude other causes

A pain plan that avoids opioid and sedative accumulation: no opioid, benzodiazepine or sleep-medicine prescription, the prescription monitoring program checked, diphenhydramine stopped, leftover medicines returned, heat and regular walking, and cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia

Depression care: cognitive behavioral therapy with the clinic's behavioral health clinician, the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 at each visit, an antidepressant to be discussed if the PHQ-9 has not fallen by half at eight to twelve weeks, a structured safety assessment and plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, and safety review at every visit

Fertility counseling: endometriosis can lower fertility, but most women with it conceive; an anti-Mullerian hormone test before any ovarian surgery; hormonal treatment does not improve fertility and is stopped when she wants to conceive; a preconception visit with folic acid; and care from reproductive endocrinology if she is not pregnant after six months of trying

Surgery held in reserve: laparoscopic excision, including removal of the endometrioma, only if the pain does not respond to medical treatment, the cyst grows, or imaging is atypical, with counseling that ovarian surgery lowers the ovarian reserve and that repeated operations should be avoided; repeat transvaginal ultrasound at about four months
Pelvic floor physical therapy for persistent deep pain with intercourse and pelvic floor muscle tenderness: down-training, manual therapy, and a home program, weekly for six to eight weeks
Worst pelvic pain 3 of 10 or less, and no missed working days for pain, by four months
Worst pain 2 of 10; no missed working days for two months
No opioid, benzodiazepine or sleep-medicine prescription, and naproxen on 10 days a month or fewer
None prescribed; naproxen on two or three days a month; diphenhydramine stopped
PHQ-9 score below 5 by four months
A written plan for when and how to try for a pregnancy, made with her before the four-month visit
Plan made: stop the pill when ready to try, after a preconception visit; reproductive endocrinology referral if not pregnant within six months

text.paragraph: Structured synthetic safety assessment on 2026-06-15: current ideation absent, intent absent, plan absent. Outpatient care. She has no thoughts of suicide or self-harm now and has never had them. Because pain, poor sleep and a moderate depressive episode raise risk, a brief written safety plan was made with her, with warning signs (feeling hopeless, not sleeping for nights at a time, wanting to use medicines to blot out the day) and what to do about each. Lethal-means counseling: no firearm at home; leftover medicines are to be returned to a pharmacy take-back site, and no opioid, benzodiazepine or sleep medicine will be prescribed. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline was given and saved in her phone, with the clinic number. Safety reviewed at every visit [S]
